speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been present and if you have noticed any fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (secondary to immunosuppression from Crohn's and Diabetes).

The patient's history of an ant bite, the progression of a painful ulcerative lesion over one month, and her significant immunocompromised state (Crohn's, diabetes, prior steroid use) are highly suggestive of a parasitic infection like Leishmaniasis, though other differentials like pyoderma gangrenosum or atypical mycobacterial infection must be considered. I will proceed with diagnostic testing to confirm. REQUEST TEST: PCR for Leishmania DNA; REQUEST TEST: Wound Culture and Biopsy for histopathology.
